questions.prompt: When using a message queue to decouple a web frontend from a backend worker, what is the primary benefit regarding request handling latency?

options.text: It reduces network bandwidth usage
It allows the frontend to respond immediately while work is processed asynchronously
It guarantees exactly-once processing
It encrypts messages in transit

questions.explanation: The frontend can enqueue a job and return a response quickly, while the worker processes it later, keeping user-facing latency low.

questions.prompt: In RabbitMQ, which exchange type routes messages to all bound queues regardless of the routing key?

options.text: Direct
Topic
Fanout
Headers

questions.explanation: A fanout exchange ignores the routing key and simply broadcasts every received message to all queues bound to it.

questions.prompt: In Apache Kafka, messages within a single partition are guaranteed to be processed in order by a consumer belonging to the same consumer group. What happens if you increase the number of consumer instances beyond the number of partitions?

options.text: Ordering is preserved across all consumers
Some consumer instances will remain idle
Messages will be duplicated
Kafka will automatically rebalance partitions to match consumer count

questions.explanation: Each partition can be assigned to only one consumer in a group; excess consumers stay idle until a partition becomes available through rebalancing.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the visibility timeout in Amazon SQS?

options.text: To encrypt messages while they are in the queue
To prevent other consumers from processing the same message for a configurable period after it is received
To automatically delete messages after they are read
To prioritize messages based on their size

questions.explanation: After a consumer receives a message, it becomes invisible to other consumers for the visibility timeout, giving the consumer time to process and delete it.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about exactly-once message processing in distributed systems is most accurate?

options.text: It can be achieved solely by using a transactional message queue without any idempotent consumer logic
Kafka provides exactly-once semantics only when using the Streams API with idempotent writes to external systems
RabbitMQ guarantees exactly-once delivery by default when using publisher confirms
SQS FIFO queues provide exactly-once processing without any additional deduplication effort

questions.explanation: Kafka's exactly-once semantics require idempotent producers and transactional writes; external systems must also be idempotent or transactional to avoid duplicates.

questions.prompt: Why would you configure a dead-letter queue (DLQ) for a message queue consumer?

options.text: To increase the throughput of the primary queue
To store messages that have exceeded the maximum receive count or failed repeatedly for later inspection
To encrypt messages before they are sent to the primary queue
To automatically reorder messages based on priority

questions.explanation: A DLQ isolates repeatedly failing messages so they don't block the main queue and can be examined to diagnose processing issues.
